objective: Let the backend (and eventually the UI) know which SSIDs a device is configured to use — SSID, priority, monotonically increasing config version — without ever writing the WiFi password to the database.

acceptance.criterion: Migration creates device_wifi_config (id, device_id, ssid, priority, config_version, updated_at + index on device_id) and applies cleanly; no password column exists.
acceptance.verification: cargo sqlx migrate run against scratch Postgres plus information_schema column check

acceptance.criterion: replace_device_wifi_config inserts with version 1, bumps to 2 on rewrite, isolates devices, and get_device_wifi_config orders by priority / returns empty for unknown devices.

POST /wifi persists SSID metadata after successful MQTT publish (DB failure logs a warning, request still succeeds); passwords never reach the DB layer; GET /wifi returns stored SSIDs + version under device:network scope.
acceptance.verification: cargo test candidates_to_ssid_entries + response-builder tests; code inspection of update_wifi_list/get_wifi_config

acceptance.criterion: No regressions: full hydragrow-backend test suite passes and cargo fmt --check is clean.
acceptance.verification: DATABASE_URL=... cargo test (full) && cargo fmt --check in hydragrow-backend
